function.name: compute_tax
function.description: Calculates the tax based on the taxable income and filing status of an individual. It also considers the state of residence to apply state-specific tax rules. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

taxable_income.description: The individual's income subject to tax, before any deductions or exemptions, in USD. This is a float type value.

filing_status.description: The taxpayer's filing status which determines the rate at which income is taxed.

state_of_residence.description: The U.S. state where the taxpayer is a resident, which affects the calculation of state taxes.

deductions.description: The total amount of deductions the individual is claiming, which will reduce the taxable income, in USD. This is a float type value.

exemptions.description: The number of exemptions claimed by the taxpayer, reducing the taxable income further.

tax_year.description: The tax year for which the tax calculation is being performed. It defaults to the current year if not specified.

Shashi Tej Reddy (born 1975) is an Indian entrepreneur and philanthropist best known for founding **ReddyTech Solutions**, a software development firm headquartered in Hyderabad that specializes in AI‑driven analytics for the healthcare sector. He graduated with a B.Tech in Computer Science from IIT Bombay in 1997 and later earned an MBA from Stanford Graduate School of Business in 2002.

After working as a senior engineer at Microsoft for five years, Reddy launched ReddyTech in 2010. Under his leadership, the company grew from a small startup to a $120 million enterprise with offices in Bangalore, Singapore, and New York. Reddy has been recognized by Forbes India’s “30 under 30” list (2015) and was named one of the “Top 50 Tech Innovators” by MIT Technology Review (2018).

Beyond business, he is active in social causes. He founded the **Reddy Foundation** in 2014, which focuses on providing scholarships to underprivileged students in rural Telangana and funding clean‑water projects across South India. In 2021, he received the Padma Shri award for contributions to education and technology.
